findings.reason: the section should be collapsed to a landed/verified claim against `reckon/crew/reports.py`, or its premise re-measured, rather than released as a node that rebuilds a check that runs.
findings.text: §22 is authored as open work ("check-manifest … does not look") but the reader it asks for already exists: `_commit_citation_findings` in `reckon/crew/reports.py:1576`, wired into `audit_manifest` at `reckon/crew/reports.py:2033`, with `tests/test_check_manifest_resolves_named_commits.py` already on disk, so the section re-specifies machinery the codebase holds

findings.reason: a duplicated resolver is the two-readers defect the plan's own §16/§38 exist to remove, so the section should route both surfaces through one resolver and name it, which changes the Files stanza and the done-when.
findings.text: the resolution predicate the plan has `check-manifest` perform ships twice: `_commit_resolves_in` in `reckon/crew/promotion.py:477` and a second, independent implementation in `reckon/crew/reports.py:1526`, each running its own `git rev-parse` probe, and the plan's §18/§22 text names neither as the owner

findings.reason: the item's own rule requires each surface-adding section to name its retirement or say why none can be, and adding that sentence to §3 and §7 is a text change the plan can make without touching the shipped behaviour.
findings.text: §7 grants the dispatch surface a new CLI option `--negative-control` (present at `reckon/cli.py:1677`) and states only that it "documents the field"; §3 likewise adds `crew watch --ensure` (present at `reckon/cli.py:5109`) with no statement of what either retires or merges, against cli_options 317

interface_budget-1.reason: sections 3 and 7 are done and their options shipped before the interface-budget rule; retiring --negative-control or crew watch --ensure is a new design question for a future section, not a change to these landed ones

reuse_search-1.reason: section 22 is done; the reader this finding cites, _commit_citation_findings wired into audit_manifest with its test, is that section's landing

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the one new module it commissions, `reckon/crew/serving_origin.py`, hides launcher query, HTTP probe and a shared wall-clock budget behind the single `check_serving_origin` call; the rest of the plan deepens existing modules rather than spreading surface.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's §18/§22 land a second commit resoler beside the one the audit path owns; two implementations of `_commit_resolves_in` now ship (`reckon/crew/promotion.py:477`, `reckon/crew/reports.py:1526`), and the plan names neither.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 1469, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §7 adds the `--negative-control` CLI option and §3 adds `crew watch --ensure`, and neither section names what it retires or merges, or states why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan names prior art where a new subsystem is proposed (§13 names `reckon/flight.py`'s endpoints reader and requires a node to justify not reusing it), and §16 names the two wait-probe readers before touching either; only §22 adds a check whose reader already exists, emitted as a finding below.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §22 adds commit-resolution to `check-manifest` as new work while the same resolution already exists as a reader on the manifest-audit path, without saying why that reader could not simply be exercised.
